import html from typing import List # Predefined HTML template with placeholders for the post's components. USER_POST_FORMAT: str = """

{heading}

Posted by: {poster}

{body}
{labels}
""" def create_forum_post(poster: str, heading: str, body: str, labels: List[str]) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML representation of a forum post. Args: poster (str): The author of the post. heading (str): The title of the user's post. body (str): The main content of the user's post. labels (List[str]): A list of tags associated with the post. Returns: str: The sanitized HTML string ready for rendering. Raises: ValueError: If any required argument is missing or not a string/list. """ # Basic type validation if not isinstance(poster, str): raise ValueError("poster must be a string") if not isinstance(heading, str): raise ValueError("heading must be a string") if not isinstance(body, str): raise ValueError("body must be a string") if not isinstance(labels, list) or any(not isinstance(l, str) for l in labels): raise ValueError("labels must be a list of strings") # Escape all user-supplied content to prevent XSS safe_poster = html.escape(poster, quote=True) safe_heading = html.escape(heading, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(body, quote=False) # body may contain newlines # Render tags as elements, escaping each tag value safe_labels = " ".join( f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in labels ) # Format the final HTML string post_html = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( poster=safe_poster, heading=safe_heading, body=safe_body.replace("\n", "
"), # preserve line breaks labels=safe_labels, ) return post_html.strip()
